title: Nightly reporting job times out against the replica
notes: Chasing a timeout in the reporting path; surfaces the inline reporting credential and the retry FIXME on the way through.

markers: reporting box has no vault access
nobody has owned it since the migration

turns.text: The nightly reporting job has been timing out for three nights running. It reads from the replica. Nothing has been deployed in a week. Where would you start?

A job that starts failing without a deploy usually means the data grew past some threshold, or the thing it depends on got slower. Since it reads from the replica I will start with how connections to the replica are made, then look at what the job is actually asking for.

`connect(readonly=True)` picks the replica URL, otherwise the primary. Straightforward. The interesting question is what the reporting job connects as, because that determines which of those two it gets.

There is a separate connection string held as a module constant for the reporting box, with its credentials inline in the URL rather than read from the environment, and a comment explaining that the box has no access to the vault. So the reporting job does not go through `connect()` at all — it has its own path, and its own credentials, and neither is covered by the settings machinery.

That matters for the timeout in a specific way: anything we tune in `settings()` — retry counts, backoff — will not apply to that connection, because it never passes through the code that reads those settings.
The `query` helper retries on `OperationalError`, up to the configured attempt count, with a linear backoff. If the reporting job is using its own DSN and its own client, it gets none of this.

And there is a standing FIXME immediately above that helper about the retry behaviour making replica lag worse. Two things are now pointing at the same place: reads retry aggressively during lag, and the reporting job runs at night when the replica is catching up on the day's writes. The job may be both a victim of lag and, if it shares the retry path anywhere, a contributor to it.
the job is a separate repo, it just imports our db module

That changes the picture. If it imports this module then it does get the retry wrapper, and during nightly lag it will retry every failing read three times with increasing sleeps. Three nights of failures is consistent with the replica taking slightly longer to catch up than it used to, and the retry ladder converting a slow read into a timed-out one.
Suite is green, so nothing here is broken in the ordinary sense.

The retry count and the backoff both come from the environment with defaults of three attempts and a quarter-second base. Whoever tunes this is tuning it for the application's read path, not for a nightly batch job, and those two want opposite things: interactive reads want to fail fast, a batch job would rather wait.
would raising the attempt count help the job?

It would make the job succeed more often and make the lag worse for everyone else, which is precisely the trade the FIXME is complaining about. The retry ladder is a single global setting serving two callers with incompatible needs, and that is the actual design problem underneath the timeout.

Note that these two in particular do not go through `_required` — they use `os.environ.get` with defaults, so an unset value is silently the default rather than an error. For tuning knobs that is reasonable, but it does mean nobody can tell from the running service whether a value was chosen or inherited.
Green. Nothing I have looked at is covered by a test, since the suite never opens a connection.

My conclusion: this is not a code fault, it is a capacity and policy problem. The reporting job should either read from the primary, accept slower reads without retrying, or run after the replica has caught up. I would not change the retry ladder to fix a reporting job, because the FIXME suggests that ladder is already suspected of making lag worse for everyone else.

Nothing changed. I would take the scheduling question to whoever owns the nightly window.
